name: Jelly Security
overview: Optional sign-in protection for Jellyfin 12.2. Playback is left alone.
description: Watches sign-in, keeps plugin-owned records, and can slow, pause, or block sign-in traffic when an administrator enables those options. Jellyfin still checks the password.

Live dashboard via Server-Sent Events: the page updates instantly when a sign-in event, ban, or incident fires. Falls back to 30s polling if SSE is unavailable.

Attack timeline: groups failed and blocked sign-in attempts by source address into chronological attack stories. Each story shows the sequence of attempts, detected patterns, and any ban applied. Read-only, built on demand from existing events.

Challenge unrecognized clients: a CAPTCHA opt-in requires a valid token from clients with no recognizable User-Agent. Automatic IPv6 /64 prefix bans: pause the whole end-user subnet instead of skipping the ban. Both off by default.
Dashboard fix: sign-in and detail tables keep short columns on one line and extend horizontally with a scrollbar instead of crushing text onto new lines.

Country blocks: an Addresses-tab table that blocks sign-in from administrator-listed country ranges. Ranges stay editable CIDR text — fill a row from the local geo file or paste a list. Enforced like a manual ban, so admin and monitoring networks stay safe.

Initial public release. 6 sign-in controls (password delay, account cooldown, lockout watch, browser challenge, honeypot ban, Quick Connect protection), 6 pattern detectors (brute force, distributed, spray, enumeration, honeypot, admin target), manual and automatic IP bans with proxy trust, session watch with non-playing device sign-out, edge proxy snippet generator (Nginx, Caddy, Cloudflare), block-list channel for proxy sync, webhook alerts with SSRF protection, backup/restore with secret redaction, dashboard with live status and active enforcement.
